source.title: Reading the Gate, Not the Interference: Output-Side Interference Measurement Does Not Track Merge Collapse

page_placements.theme: Restoration at the level of residual-stream features, directions or activation geometry (not component outputs)

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper explicitly distinguishes its cross-term regeneration from attention-component self-repair. It does not ablate attention layers or heads or test the claim versions’ output-restoration behavior.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses Hydra and Explorations of Self-Repair, but says its intervention concerns a four-path cross-term coordinate rebuilt from untouched marginal paths, not compensation after ablating a transformer component. The reported cross-term regrowth is recorded as a related but different finding, not as evidence for a claim version.
record.test_reason: The paper studies a factorial activation cross-term in task-arithmetic merged models. It erases that cross-term at a residual boundary and tracks whether it regrows. It never ablates attention layers, heads or MLPs, and never measures output restoration after removing a component. Appendix G says outright that its regeneration is 'a different object' from Hydra-style self-repair. Self-repair is discussed only for comparison, so no version of the claim is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the regrowth aside, though it is accurate there. The paper's main conclusion is different. Output-side interference measures in merged models track the instruction-format gate, the denominator and the displacement budget, not interference itself. In collapse the activation cross-term is a bystander: erasing it repairs nothing. State-space measures rank merging methods correctly where the output-side ratio does not. On the side point, the authors say regrowth is coordinate regeneration distinct from Hydra-style self-repair. They also say how much known self-repair mechanisms explain it remains open.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention erases a factorial activation cross-term at a chosen residual-stream boundary; it is not attention-layer or head ablation.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-term recovery depends on erasure depth: the reported final-boundary recovery ratio falls from 1.000 at depth 3 to 0.843 at depth 20.

fits_no_version.finding: After the cross-term is erased with λ=1, the final-boundary recovery ratio ρ is 1.000, 0.992, 0.944 and 0.843 for erasure at depths 3, 8, 14 and 20. Direction cosine to the original is about 0.99 at depth 8. The durable output effect D is about 0 for early erasure and positive only for late erasure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In merged LLMs, an erased four-path cross-term coordinate is regenerated from the untouched marginal paths, in both norm and direction, unless it is erased near the output.

fits_no_version.finding: Basin test: from every start (correct erasure and four norm-matched controls at depths 8 and 14), the downstream cross-term direction reconverges, with cosines of 0.83 to 0.99 in 18/18 cells. Appendix N finds that the perturbed state never rejoins its unperturbed trajectory, and that no restoring force is specific to the cross-term direction (frozen prediction failed, 0/3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Propagation restores a differential coordinate, not the model state. This is distinct from component-ablation self-repair of an output prediction.

record.problems: The paper does not directly test any claim version. Its related cross-term-regrowth results concern a different intervention and target; the reported regrowth scope is 18 cells across three seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No component-ablation or output-restoration results were reported. Other cross-term-erasure outcomes, including behavioral-collapse repair tests, do not measure the behaviors named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No attention-layer ablation and no measurement of later-layer compensation of the output.
No late-MLP analysis and no erasure of the maximum-likelihood token.
No single-head ablation on general text or across model families.
No per-prompt distribution of compensation after component ablation, and no test of overcorrection.
No tests of backup heads, copy-suppression heads, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons. LayerNorm's share of the cross-term regrowth is explicitly left open (App. G).
No comparison of zero, mean or resample component ablation.
No test of whether ablation-based importance scores misstate what a component does.

record.verdict_notes: Rows R1–R4 are correctly unlinked; their values match Appendix G. The intervention is a norm-matched activation edit toward an additive counterfactual in LoRA-merged Qwen2.5-1.5B, not removal of a component. Self-repair papers are cited only to set this work apart from them.

versions.untested_parts: No attention-layer ablation or later-attention-layer compensation test.
No late-MLP counterbalancing or maximum-likelihood-token erasure test.
No single-head ablation or full-distribution self-repair test.
No prompt-level distribution of component-ablation compensation or overcorrection.
No tests of backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final-LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons.
No test of how component-ablation importance scores relate to a component’s function.

relation.reason: Appendix G explicitly compares regeneration with prior self-repair findings and distinguishes the recovered differential coordinate from output restoration.

tranche.reason: Cross-term regeneration measures a different construct from component-ablation compensation in V1–V7; the study neither tests nor uses those claims.

source_check.notes: Appendix G reports basin-test per-condition mean cosines of 0.90–0.99 and a worst single cell of 0.83. Appendix N finds no privileged restoring force for the cross-term direction; these results do not establish any listed self-repair version.
